tab.intro: Configure how Pivot activates and how much extra yaw or pitch it can add for each title. Use profiles to keep rotation behavior specific to the games and simulators that benefit from it.
tab.defaultProfileScope: Applies to applications without an enabled custom profile
tab.defaultProfileOffNote: Off unless an enabled custom profile turns it on. Custom profiles below still apply to their applications.
tab.customProfilesIntro: Override Pivot per application. Profiles for the same title can use different bindings; the binding you press picks the profile, and order sets priority.
tab.noCustomProfiles: No custom profiles yet. Add a profile to bind Pivot rotation to a specific application.

warnings.noActivationMessage: Motion Assist will remain off until you add a Toggle or Hold binding, or enable Always active. Compatible Snap View profiles remain available.
warnings.bothAlwaysActive: Both this profile and "{owner}" are Always active for {app}. The higher-priority profile engages first; use activation controls when you need predictable switching.
warnings.profileNoActivation: Motion Assist has no activation bindings and will remain off. Add a Toggle or Hold binding, or enable Always active. Compatible Snap View profiles remain available.
warnings.bindingOwnedAlwaysOn: For {app}, binding {binding} is owned by the higher-priority "{owner}" (Profile {number}). Always On still engages automatically, but this binding cannot suspend or resume it. Other unshadowed bindings still work.

compatibility.title: A Special Note About Quadviews
compatibility.managed: VectorXR Quadviews is fully compatible with Pivot and Depth when all three modules are managed by VectorXR.
compatibility.runtime: Pivot is NOT currently compatible with quadviews supplied directly by the runtime, such as Pimax Play.
compatibility.external: Pivot also works with external OpenXR quadviews layers, including mbucchia's `Quad-Views-Foveated`, when layer order is configured correctly.
compatibility.layerOrder: When using quadviews, OpenXR layer order matters. `Quad-Views-Foveated` should be first in the Windows OpenXR API layers list, with VectorXR second. If VectorXR is above the quadviews layer, Pivot rotation will cause the scene to break, rendering no content in areas outside your head's natural field of view.
compatibility.layerManager: You can inspect and change that order with the OpenXR Layer Manager tab in VectorXR.

centering.title: Keeping Pivot Aligned
centering.center: Pivot rotates around your headset's center point, not the game's. These are two separate concepts of "forward," and by default Pivot uses the HMD one.
centering.drift: If Pivot rotation feels off-center or skewed to one side, your HMD center and your in-game center have drifted apart.
centering.bestFix: The best fix: assign the optional {setOrigin} binding (under Origin Controls) to the same button you use to recenter the view in-game. Every recenter then updates both origins together, so they can never drift apart.
centering.manual: Without a Set Origin binding, you can re-align manually: recenter your HMD first, then recenter your view in the game. Doing both, in that order, re-aligns the two centers so Pivot rotates evenly around where you are actually looking.

units.degreesHardDeadzone: degrees · 0 keeps the original hard deadzone

advancedAxes.label: Advanced axes — tune each direction independently
advancedAxes.continuousDescription: Separate multiplier, deadzone, and cap for looking left, right, up, and down. Enabling this starts each direction from your current yaw/pitch values.
advancedAxes.steppedDescription: Give left, right, up, and down separate deadzones, triggers, amounts, hysteresis, and limits.

fields.responseModeHint: Continuous scales your head rotation smoothly with a multiplier. Stepped adds fixed chunks of rotation as your head crosses angle thresholds, like XRNeckSafer's stepped mode.
fields.smoothingHint: Low-pass filter on continuous pivot response for both yaw and pitch. 0 = instant, higher = smoother but laggier. Good range: 0.05–0.2.
fields.activationRampHint: Seconds to ease the pivot effect in and out when you toggle it on or off, so activating it never snaps the view. 0 = instant. Default 0.35.
fields.deadzoneTransitionHint:
Eases from 1:1 to full sensitivity over this many degrees beyond the deadzone, instead of switching at its edge. 0 keeps the original hard deadzone.

For example, with an 8° deadzone and an 8° transition, amplification starts gently at 8° and reaches full strength at 16°.

The gentler start gives up half the transition width × (multiplier − 1) of extra rotation: at ×1.5 with an 8° transition, the view stays 2° behind a hard deadzone until Max Extra is reached.
fields.yawMultiplierHint: Amplifies head yaw (left/right) beyond the deadzone. 1.0 = no change. 1.3–2.0 is typical; up to 3 helps look further or behind you depending on your headset and head-tracking range.
fields.yawMaxExtraHint: Cap on the extra yaw degrees pivot can add on top of natural head movement. 180° lets you look directly behind you.
fields.yawDeadzoneHint: Degrees of head yaw ignored before amplification kicks in. Prevents jitter when looking straight ahead. 2–8° is typical.
fields.pitchMultiplierHint: Amplifies head pitch (up/down) beyond the deadzone. 1.0 = no change. 1.2–2.0 is typical; up to 3 helps look over the nose or up at the canopy.
fields.pitchMaxExtraHint: Cap on the extra pitch degrees pivot can add. Useful for looking over the nose or up at the canopy without craning your neck.
fields.pitchDeadzoneHint: Degrees of head pitch ignored before amplification kicks in. 2–12° is typical.
fields.directionMultiplierHint: How much head rotation is amplified in this direction after the deadzone. 1.0 adds no extra rotation.
fields.directionDeadzoneHint: Head rotation in this direction that is ignored before Motion starts adding rotation.
fields.directionMaxExtraHint: The most extra rotation Motion can add in this direction.
fields.yawLeftHint: Applied when turning your head to the left.
fields.yawRightHint: Applied when turning your head to the right.
fields.pitchUpHint: Applied when tilting your head up.
fields.pitchDownHint: Applied when tilting your head down.

activation.baselineActive: Pivot starts active. Bindings below suspend it instead of activating it.
activation.baselineInactive: Pivot starts inactive and is controlled by the activation bindings below.
activation.noSuspendBindings: No suspend bindings assigned. Enhanced Motion remains active for the whole session.
activation.noActivationBindings: No activation binding assigned. Enhanced Motion cannot be activated until one is added.
activation.suspendToggle: Press once to suspend Enhanced Motion; press again to resume.
activation.suspendHold: Hold to suspend Enhanced Motion; release to resume.
activation.activateToggle: Press once to activate Enhanced Motion; press again to deactivate.
activation.activateHold: Enhanced Motion stays active only while this control is held.
activation.noSuspendControl: No suspend control assigned for this slot.
activation.noActivationControl: No activation control assigned for this slot.

positionAssist.title: Position Assist
positionAssist.description: Add lean or height as you turn. Physical leaning remains 1:1. Offsets ease in and out, level with the horizon and facing your seated Pivot origin.
positionAssist.startingPointsDetail: Gentle leans 12 cm toward the turn and rises 4 cm between 20° and 70° of head turn, enough to see past the seat when checking six. Strong leans 20 cm and rises 8 cm between 15° and 60°. Keep Start angle beyond your normal panel scan so glances stay still, and set Full-offset angle near where you stop turning. A preset replaces every direction; Advanced directions get no up/down movement.
positionAssist.presetNoneTitle: Clears every offset and restores the default angles.
positionAssist.presetGentleTitle: 12 cm lean toward the turn and 4 cm up, between 20° and 70° of head turn.
positionAssist.presetStrongTitle: 20 cm lean toward the turn and 8 cm up, between 15° and 60° of head turn.
positionAssist.advancedDirections: Advanced directions — independent left, right, up, and down
positionAssist.anglesOutOfOrder: Full-offset angle must be greater than Start angle.
positionAssist.footnote: Uses physical head angle. Inside a stacked Snap View, movement is measured around its captured head reference and the offsets face the snapped view. Negative offsets reverse the movement.

stepped.stepGlideDescription: Instant jumps directly to each step. Glide moves monotonically to the new target without overshoot or coasting.
stepped.transitionHint: Choose whether each new step is applied immediately or eased in over the set duration.
stepped.durationHint: How many seconds a Glide transition takes to reach its new step target. This is shared by every direction.
stepped.durationInstant: seconds — Instant has no transition time

stepTuning.deadzoneHint: The base head angle before step thresholds begin. Motion inside this angle never creates a step.
stepTuning.stepTriggerHint: How many more degrees you turn after the deadzone to add each step.
stepTuning.stepAmountHint: How much extra view rotation is added each time you cross a step trigger.
stepTuning.hysteresisHint: How far you must turn back below a trigger before its step is removed. This prevents flicker near a threshold and must be smaller than Step Trigger.
stepTuning.hysteresisInvalid: must be smaller than step trigger
stepTuning.maxExtraHint: The most extra view rotation these steps can add. Set to 0 for no cap.

motionSource.hardwareUnavailableCards: No graphics card in this PC has NVIDIA's optical flow hardware ({cards}).
motionSource.hardwareUnavailable: No graphics card in this PC has NVIDIA's optical flow hardware.
motionSource.lockedNote: In Dynamic, Interpolate measures motion with Shader: its frames between real frames need motion sooner than the NVIDIA hardware delivers it beside a busy game. The choice applies to Extrapolate, and to Interpolate at a fixed or Auto frame rate.
motionSource.hardwareMissingNote: NVIDIA hardware is chosen, but no graphics card here has it, so Shader measures motion.
motionSource.experimentalNote: Experimental: Interpolate measures motion with the NVIDIA hardware at a fixed or Auto frame rate. If its motion arrives late, Frame Generation runs a refresh further ahead (more latency); Shader is the safe choice.
